description.narrative: The Mozambican Stratigraphic Nomenclature Project (MSNP) aims to develop and publish together with the National Petroleum Institute (INP), Empresa Nacional Hydrocarbons (ENH) and Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM) regionally applicable stratigraphic units (lithostratigraphic nomenclature). A central part of this effort is to train and coach the staff of INP and ENH, enabling them to develop and maintain a national stratigraphic nomenclator.This project aims to enhance the good governance and understanding of the Mozambican subsurface, allowing for maximizing revenues from its natural resources while at the same time minimizing risk.

comment.narrative:
Capacity building and coaching to 16 policy officers coming from the technical teams of the Instituto Nacional de Petróleo (INP) and the national oil company, Empresa Nacional de Hidrocarbonatos (ENH) of Mozambique on geoscientific work for the development and maintenance of a national stratigraphic nomenclature. The training included four practical workshops (of four days each) and a multitude of bi weekly virtual meetings/course hours.
From INP 8 policy officers (including 1 female geoscientist). From ENH also 1 policy officers (including 2 female geoscientist).
The knowledge transfer and capacity building has taken place in the form of on-the job training, short courses, and workshops. This included practical skills using industry software (e.g. seismic interpretation, well log correlation and geographical information); how to use the bio-stratigraphical analysis to build a stratigraphic framework. And finally the synthesis of all data and information gathered into the stratigraphic nomenclature.The participants also developed professional skills to apply technical knowledge in industry and business processes.

comment.narrative:
1 Government: Instituto Nacional de Petróleo (INP) INP has been established to manage and oversee Mozambique's petroleum resources and is responsible for the regulation and control of research relating to exploration for and production and transportation of petroleum; the preservation of public interest and the environment in the sector; the administration, maintenance and publishing of technical information and data relating to the activities of the petroleum industry; participating in the establishment of concession areas and related concession contracts; and overseeing and ensuring legal and regulatory compliance of petroleum operations.
2 Semi-government: Empresa Nacional de Hidrocarbonatos (ENH, national oil company) The Petroleum Law provides that ENH will represent the State in petroleum operations. ENH participates in both upstream and midstream petroleum operations including exploration, production, refining, transportation, storage and commercialisation of oil and gas and their by-products (including LNG and GTL), both inside and/or outside Mozambique. ENH is also responsible for managing the required quotas in respect of oil and gas to be channelled to the domestic market. Finally, any investor interested in exploiting the petroleum resources of Mozambique must enter into a partnership with ENH, as the representative of the State.
3 Other; International petroleum industry active in Mozambique and more indirectly eventually this will reach Mozambican universities

title.narrative: Description of changes achieved in laws, regulations, policy plans, outcomes of social dialogue or development strategies enacted or adopted by local government or social dialogue partners, yielding tangible benefits to the business climate

comment.narrative:
The project enabled knowledge transfer from TNO Netherlands to the government of Mozambique (INP and ENH) through capacity building on geological knowledge infrastructure for the development of regionally applicable stratigraphic nomenclature; which enables the business climate in the gas sector, which has a large potential for development in teh country. A formal and standard stratigraphic nomenclature strengthen the position of the government of Mozambique in their communication and negotiation with industry stakeholders.
The project has contributed to the development of a Stratigraphic Nomenclature for Mozambique that could also be applicable in other countries in the south east African region. This stratigraphic nomenclature describes the lithological units in Mozambique based on tectono-stratigraphic, sequence-stratigraphic and bio-stratigraphic properties. The work focused on the stratigraphy of the Zambesi Delta Area (ZDA) and the Rovuma Basin (RB) offshore the Northern coast of Mozambique. For the ZDA the stratigraphic nomenclature was fully developed. The work was primarily be based on existing data (mainly coming from the oil and gas industry) and published (scientific) papers and reports. The stratigraphic nomenclature for the RB was not fully finalized and the final report is pending due to limitation of time. An international stratigraphic integration for the RB that extends across the Mozambican–Tanzanian border was developed based on scientific publications; which is included in the final report.
This strategraphic nomenclature provides technical input for the formal adoption of the nomenclature and the development of legal regulation by the Mozambican government.
